name: twitter-x

# Twitter / X

Treat X as a public conversation channel, not a broadcast schedule. Build around one useful idea at a time: an observation, decision, lesson, demonstration, or credible point of view.

## Start from the task

Identify:

- the campaign role: awareness, feedback, proof, conversation, or conversion;
- the intended reader and what they already know;
- the project facts, examples, results, screenshots, and voice samples available;
- whether the deliverable is a strategy, todo plan, post, thread, quote reply, or revision.

Ask for missing facts only when they are necessary. Otherwise narrow the claim or mark a placeholder. Never invent product usage, customer results, personal experience, quotes, or metrics.

## Build the channel strategy

Choose a small set of repeatable content jobs that fit the project, such as:

- build log: a real decision, tradeoff, failure, or change;
- useful observation: a specific pattern the audience can apply;
- product proof: show a workflow, before/after, or concrete capability;
- resource or teardown: teach with an example rather than a generic list;
- conversation: respond to a relevant claim with a distinct contribution.

For each content job, define its audience, evidence source, format, intended response, and connection to the project. Set cadence from the user's capacity and observed results. Present timing, frequency, and format choices as testable hypotheses, not universal algorithm rules.

Do not prescribe mass replies, engagement pods, automated likes, bulk follows, duplicate posts, or unsolicited automated DMs.

## Turn strategy into todos

Make every todo a finishable deliverable. Include:

- what will be produced;
- the source material or proof to use;
- the intended reader and purpose;
- the required format;
- a clear completion check.

Avoid vague todos such as “engage with the community.” For a reply task, name the type of conversation to find and require a paste-ready reply draft. For a test, change one meaningful variable and define what will be reviewed afterward.

## Write publish-ready content

### Single post

Lead with the strongest specific point. Make the post understandable without hidden context. Use short paragraphs only when they improve reading. Add a link, mention, hashtag, or CTA only when it serves the reader and the task.

### Thread

Use a thread only when the idea genuinely needs sequence. Open with the subject and value, not an empty teaser. Give each post one clear job. Make transitions carry the argument forward. End with the conclusion or next action rather than repeating the opening.

### Quote reply or reply

Respond to the actual claim. Add evidence, a useful distinction, a question, or a relevant example. Do not manufacture agreement, outrage, or familiarity. If the source post is unavailable, provide a reply template with the missing context clearly marked instead of pretending to have read it.

## Match the user's voice

Prefer wording supported by the user's writing samples. Preserve their language, level of certainty, and attitude toward the audience. Remove generic thought-leadership openings, inflated claims, fake vulnerability, slogan chains, and unexplained jargon.

Use a CTA proportionate to the content. A useful observation may need no CTA; a feedback post may ask one focused question; a product proof post may point to the product when the connection is natural.

## Revise without drifting

When revising, identify the exact criticism and change only what it requires. Preserve verified facts, intended audience, and deliverable format. Do not silently introduce a new strategy, claim, or persona. If feedback conflicts with evidence or platform rules, explain the conflict and offer a safe alternative.

## Check before delivery

Confirm that:

- every factual claim is supported or clearly qualified;
- the draft has one main point and a recognizable reader;
- the output is paste-ready for the requested format;
- no tactic depends on artificial amplification, duplication, or unsolicited automation;
- mutable platform limits or automation capabilities are verified at execution time.

Use the current official rules when platform behavior matters:

- X Rules: https://help.x.com/en/rules-and-policies/x-rules
- X Automation Rules: https://help.x.com/en/rules-and-policies/x-automation
